coaching.headline: Every lane was won or held even, and the game still finished 7 majors to 25 and 1 tower to 10.
coaching.team:
The draft gave the team every lane won or held even: the carry lane, the offlane, the midlane and the jungle all favored, and the support lane dead level. The early game matched that promise. The team won a clean skirmish in the river at 2.9, Kira started picking off Skylar in lane, and a 2-0 fight at 13.3 converted straight into Mini Prime, the team's only cashed win of the game.

The map read was worse than the fights alone suggest. The other team controlled the river buffs 19 to 5 and both seedlings, destroyed six of the team's wards while losing none of their own, and took the first Fangtooth uncontested at minute 10 with the whole roster alive and nobody near it.

From minute 15 on, the fights stopped going the team's way. At 15.9, a push on their outer tower was taken without the support in it and went 1-3, costing two towers and the next Fangtooth in the minutes that followed. At 22.5, only two players answered a fight near the team's own Fangtooth and lost it 0-2, costing an inner tower a minute later. The real break came at 23.3, when Feng Mao was caught alone by Serath. Forty seconds later the team's next fight opened four bodies against five before a hit landed. It went 1-4 and cost two inner towers and an inhibitor in the same stretch. Everything after that was fought from behind, with Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime both conceded with a teammate already dead.

The support was alive and out of position for ten of the team's fourteen clustered fights, and the offlane, usually ahead in its own lane, was missing from nine. The one thing to fix next game is simple: get the whole roster to the fight before it starts.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What actually turned a favored draft into a 1-tower loss? Two compounding things. First, the support and the offlane were both alive and simply out of most of the team's fights: the support missed 10 of the team's 14 clustered fights, the offlane missed 9, and the costliest losses are the ones they missed. Second, the catch on Feng Mao at 23.3 turned the very next engagement into a 4-vs-5 before it started; that single fight, lost 1-4, cost two inner towers and an inhibitor and put the team too far behind to recover.
coaching.whatWorked: Kira was the one clear strength: she picked off Skylar six separate times through the lane and early game. She also anchored the team's best fight of the match at 13.3, a 2-0 win that is the only one of the team's three won fights actually converted into an objective, Mini Prime. The other two wins were left on the table without a prize to show for it.

His solo catch by Serath at 23.3 is the costliest single death of the game: forty seconds later the team fought its most damaging loss of the match a body down.

From there survival wasn't the issue; being in the fight was. The offlane was alive and ahead in its lane for nine of the team's fourteen clustered fights and only joined five of them.

But staying alive isn't the same as showing up: he was out of ten of the team's fourteen clustered fights, including the 15.9 loss at their outer tower and the 17.1 loss at their Fangtooth that followed it. For a support, the yardstick is map presence, and that's the piece that was missing most of the game.

A carry's value shows up in whether the team converts around her, and the individual dominance here never quite turned into map progress.

24.call: Feng Mao's solo catch forty seconds earlier meant this fight opened 4-5 before a hit landed, and it ended 1-4, taking two inner towers and an inhibitor with it. The call was to recognize the numbers were already lost and disengage rather than commit into a losing headcount at the tower.

13.3.call: This is the one time the team converted a fight win into a prize: a clean 2-0 near the buff, right as Mini Prime came online.

15.9.call: Taken without the support in the fight, it went 1-3 at their outer tower, costing two towers and the next Fangtooth in the minutes that followed. The call here was to wait for the fifth body or disengage. A tower push isn't worth forcing without the full roster attached.

20.5.call: Five versus five in open river with nothing immediately on the line, and it went 1-4. Fangtooth landed in the same stretch, which softened the loss, but a fight with no prize up wasn't worth taking on an even coin flip.

22.5.call: Only two players were in position to answer this fight near the team's own Fangtooth, and it went 0-2. Both deaths fed the inner tower a minute later, and three teammates were alive and elsewhere when the fight started, which makes this a map-presence read more than a duel one.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy's three finished items leaned into poke and answering Mourn's healing: Soulbinder's bonus damage at long range and Tainted Scepter's anti-heal-and-ramping-damage proc. He never reached the meta core of Azure Core, Entropy and Overseer, completing only three of six intended items. Entropy's guaranteed on-hit magic damage and Azure Core's low-health shield are the pieces that keep a mage alive through a long fight, and their absence lines up with eight deaths, five of which handed the other team a tower or an objective soon after. Against Grux and Serath, both dive-capable, the missing shield was the one that would have mattered most.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Demiurge is the modeled top pick for Gadget, rewarding a full six-item build with extra stats from items and bonus damage from item effects; the default minors add health-and-haste scaling per level plus more damage and mitigation for every item owned. That's a late-game engine pick, trading away the earlier ability-damage poke route for one that needs the inventory finished to pay off. Gadget completed only three of his six items this game, so that payoff window never really arrived.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Feng Mao's build was close to the meta core, missing only Omen. Manta Scythe took its place, trading Omen's stack-up cooldown reduction and empowered basic for bonus damage against isolated targets, suited to solo duels. What the build skipped entirely was any defensive stat, and the matchup flag says as much: no armor against a three-physical-damage lineup. That shows up in the result, nine deaths, the most on the team, including the solo catch by Serath at 23.3 that started the game's costliest fight.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Demiurge is also the modeled top pick for Feng Mao, the same item-stat and item-effect-damage scaling Gadget runs, built around a finished six-item inventory. It trades away the tankier, health-stacking route a jungle duelist could lean on to survive dives and keep trading. Feng Mao finished only three items and died nine times, the most on the team, so like Gadget the build's late payoff never arrived.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: There's no meta-core reference for Scarlett in this data, so the read is against her own optimizer path: Basilisk, Viper, The Perforator and Augmentation for armor shred and on-hit burst. What she actually built, Tainted Guard, Overlord, Terminus and Syonic Echo, is a durability-and-anti-heal set instead: armor and health from Tainted Guard and Overlord, lifesteal converted to a shield from Terminus. As the team's only listed frontline, and the player who took the most damage on the roster, leaning into survival over damage was a defensible read, even if it skipped the more aggressive path the optimizer wants.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Krix is the modeled top pick for Scarlett, a health-stacking major that also grows her hitbox, paired here with an anti-heal proc on her damage-over-time hits and bonus health per takedown. That anti-heal minor lines up directly with Mourn's healing on the other team. It trades away the burst-oriented, item-scaling route that was her next-best-fitting option, leaning fully into durability for the team's only frontline instead of damage.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Maco's three items, Hexbound Bracers, Gaia Greaves and Everbloom, are a personal-sustain set: mana return and reduced basic-attack damage, armor and stacked movement-based damage, and mitigation plus tenacity on healing an ally. None of the meta core of Crescelia, Enra's Blessing and Windcaller made it in, and Enra's Blessing specifically shields an ally who has been locked down, a direct answer to the pull-and-knockup chain the enemy comp carried. Maco led the team in assists and stayed alive, though the build is built around his own survival rather than shielding a teammate who gets caught.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vesh is the modeled top pick for Maco, adding a damage-over-time to his ability hits, with minors that grant haste on takedowns and extra bite against high-health targets. It's an ability-damage poke archetype built more for chipping a fight than peeling it, the damage-scaling support style rather than the peel style. Maco spent much of the game alive but out of the team's fights, which a damage-focused kit does less to fix than a presence-and-peel one would.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Kira finished four of her intended six items, tied with Scarlett for the most complete build on the team, all leaning into pressure: Tainted Rounds' anti-heal, Ruination's mana-punish bleed, and Imperator's critical damage. The missing meta pieces, Solaris and Ashbringer, are a self-healing on-hit proc and a cooldown refund on basics, survivability and uptime rather than raw damage. That tracks with the game: she was the team's most dominant individual threat, picking off Skylar six separate times, but still went down six times herself, four of those deaths feeding a tower loss soon after.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Demiurge is the modeled strongest fit among Kira's options, an item-stat and item-effect-damage scaler built around a finished six-item inventory, with the default minors adding per-level health and haste plus more damage and mitigation for every item owned. It leans fully into her marksman damage scaling rather than the survivability her kit lacks. She got closer to a finished build than anyone else on the team, which tracks with her being the top individual performer, but the loadout added damage rather than survivability, and six deaths in the loss show that gap.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull), Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
